meta.sourceStandard: College Board CED, 9 units — this pilot ports only Unit 1 (of 9)
meta.purpose: Second course pilot proving the ICourseModule architecture is genuinely course-agnostic, not CS-A-specific. Scoped to a single unit deliberately (see BUILD-PLAN.md): The Global Tapestry, c. 1200-1450, covering regional state-building across Africa, the Americas, Asia, and Europe before sustained Afro-Eurasian-American contact, plus the interregional trade/belief-system threads that connect those regions. No history-appropriate scene primitives (timeline/map/cause-effect) exist yet, so every node below uses viz:"none" as a placeholder rather than a fake primitive name nothing renders; building those primitives is future work, not part of this pilot.

nodes.title: Framing the period: periodization c. 1200-1450 and comparison as a historical thinking skill
State-building in West Africa: Mali's imperial administration under Mansa Musa
Trans-Saharan trade routes and the spread of Islam through West African commercial centers
State-building in the Americas: Mexica and Inca imperial systems
Tribute collection and agricultural adaptation: chinampas and terracing without Afro-Eurasian contact
State-building in East Asia: Song China's bureaucratic centralization
Neo-Confucianism and the civil service examination system as tools of imperial administration
State-building in South Asia: the Delhi Sultanate and religious pluralism under Muslim rule
State-building in Europe: feudal decentralization and the Catholic Church's parallel authority
Interregional trade infrastructure: the Silk Roads, Indian Ocean network, and trans-Saharan routes as connective tissue
Comparing belief systems as organizing structures for governance: Islam, Christianity, Buddhism, and Confucianism
Environmental and demographic patterns before sustained contact: agricultural surplus, urbanization, and regional disease environments
Synthesis: compare state-building strategies across two or more regions, c. 1200-1450
